# MLS coverage ledger

Initial inventory: 2026-10-08 America/New_York. Source: Murray, Li, and Sastry,
*A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation* (the PDF is not part of this repository).
This starts the inventory step in the [library roadmap](lean-library-roadmap.md).
See [geometry conventions](geometry-conventions.md) for the coordinate contract.

## Scope and counting

This is a **selected-item inventory**, not a full-book inventory. The original
59 obligations (28 rotation, 15 rigid-transform, and 16 selected kinematics
rows) retain their IDs. The I3 source review adds 63 rows, X01-X63, for twists,
rigid exponentials, screws, velocities, adjoints, wrenches, and reciprocal systems
from Chapter 2 pp39-69, giving 122 selected rows through I5.
[I6](#implementation-evidence-i6) adds four bounded Appendix A rows, L01-L04,
so the current selected denominator is 126; this is not an estimate of the
book's total content. The X rows were all Unverified at I3; I4 checks 36,
I5 adds 11, and I6 adds 15 more. X60 retains a checked conditional result and
remains Unverified as a whole row. Source inventory is separate from proof evidence.
Raw check outputs (build logs, axiom audits, instance files) are kept in the maintainers'
development records outside the repository; the published evidence anchor is the commit named
in each row or in its implementation-evidence section.

Definitions, structures, theorems, specifications, and derived bridges have
distinct labels. Each stable ID names one selected obligation; one source
proposition may require several Lean lemmas, and one implementation theorem may
support several statements. Counts measure selected obligations, not independent
theorems, implementation effort, or book coverage. No full-book percentage is
justified. The [I1 evidence](#implementation-evidence-i1) supports 21 obligations,
[I2](#implementation-evidence-i2) adds six, and
[I3](#implementation-evidence-i3) adds R13-R18, giving 33 through I3.
[I4](#implementation-evidence-i4) adds 36, giving 69 through I4.
[I5](#implementation-evidence-i5) adds 15, giving 84 through I5.

Pages are `printed / PDF`, with PDF pages one-based. All inspected main-text
pages satisfy PDF page = printed page + 18. Source reading and rendering do not
establish a Lean result. A Verified row must identify the declaration, assumptions,
pinned toolchain, and check. User acceptance is separate.

## Representation and module map

Names below are intended targets unless accompanied by implementation evidence.
The initial representation is
`RoboLean.Vec3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`,
`RoboLean.Rotation := Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin 3) ℝ`, and a
`RoboLean.RigidTransform` with rotation and translation fields. Matrix action
uses `Matrix.toEuclideanLin`; public actions are `Rotation.act`,
`RigidTransform.applyPoint`, and `RigidTransform.applyVector`. The default norm
on a Pi coordinate type must not silently replace Euclidean norm. Frame indices and separate point/vector types
are deferred; the named actions retain their distinct meanings.

| Alias | Intended module | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RT | `RoboLean/Geometry/RigidTransform.lean` | Initial rotation and rigid-transform API |
| H | `RoboLean/Geometry/Homogeneous.lean` | Pair/homogeneous-matrix bridge |
| CP | `RoboLean/Geometry/CrossProduct.lean` | Euclidean cross product and proper-rotation/vector preservation |
| HT | `RoboLean/Geometry/Hat.lean` | Hat/vee, skew-matrix linear equivalence, rotation conjugation |
| HP | `RoboLean/Geometry/HatPowers.lean` | Euclidean hat square/cube identities |
| RD | `RoboLean/Geometry/Rodrigues.lean` | Rodrigues equalities for the actual matrix exponential |
| X | `RoboLean/Geometry/Twist.lean` | Two-field twist structure (`linear`, `angular`) with componentwise real vector space; independent twist matrix carrier and hat/vee linear equivalence |
| SE | `RoboLean/Geometry/TwistExp.lean` | Actual rigid exponential; closed forms, normalization, and translation-coefficient invertibility in companion modules |

Coordinates are real columns in right-handed orthonormal frames. `g_ab` sends B
coordinates to A; `g_ab * g_bc` applies `g_bc` first. For `g=(p,R)`, point action
is `p+Rq`, vector action is `Rv`, and distances are Euclidean. Twists use `(v,ω)`.
These conventions interpret code; they do not certify measured frame labels.

The pair definition and homogeneous equivalence do not characterize every
distance- and cross-product-preserving map as such a pair. That converse remains
un-inventoried; R09/T14 separately track cross-product preservation by the
coordinate action. Named fields are `rotation`, `translation`, while MLS writes
the mathematical pair `(p,R)`.

Supporting action/inner-product lemmas do not inflate this inventory. Example 2.1
(pp. 38–39) is row T19. The later fixed-line
examples are explicitly inventoried in X14-X15 below and remain Unverified. The current exact quarter-turn composition
probe is a convention check, not a substitute for that example or Chapter 3 FK.

## Twist, adjoint, and wrench obligations, Chapter 2

The I3 source review
opened every rendered printed page pp39-69/PDF57-87. These 63 new rows comprise
20 definitions, 36 theorem obligations, and seven bridges. All were Unverified
at I3; I4 supports 36 full rows, I5 adds 11, and I6 adds 15, giving 62 full
X rows. X60 retains a certificate-conditional check and remains Unverified
as a whole source obligation.
The preserved proposal
records the original source inventory and page-inspection commands.

Module labels now follow the checked I4 implementation: X = `Geometry/Twist.lean`,
SE = `Geometry/TwistExp.lean` and its closed-form/Jacobian companions,
SV = `Geometry/RotationVelocity.lean`, `Geometry/RigidVelocity.lean`, and their
trajectory/composition companions, AD = `Geometry/TwistAdjoint.lean`, and
WR = `Geometry/Wrench.lean`. EX names selected examples. SC has a checked
attribute layer in `Geometry/TwistScrew.lean`; coordinate reciprocal systems
are in `Geometry/Reciprocal.lean`. Geometric screw and axis rows retain their
individual statuses. All paths are beneath `RoboLean/`. The homogeneous index
is `Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1`; twist order is `(v,ω)` and wrench order is `(f,τ)`.

### Gaps retained after this inventory

- These are selected obligations, not a full-book denominator and not independent
  Lean theorem counts. Multi-display propositions remain single source
  obligations where they state one relationship. The chapter-2 worked examples
  are selected as convention/derivative checks, not presumed substitutes for
  chapter-3 kinematic semantics.
- No bracket definition or theorem occurs on Chapter 2 pp39-69. I6 adds four
  separately sourced Appendix A rows below for the coordinate bracket, matrix
  bridge, Lie identities, and derived adjoint covariance. A manifold/tangent
  identification or general vector-field theory is not claimed.
- I6 supplies actual affine axes, independent finite/pure-translation screw
  motion, and explicit zero twist/wrench policies. The common-normal certificate's existence, the `atan2` angle and the parallel and infinite-pitch cases were added in [I39](#implementation-evidence-i39).
- I6 defines a global noncomputable selected principal twist. Smoothness or
  uniqueness of that choice, global Euler coordinates, manifold interfaces, full exercise coverage, typed frames/units,
  numerical refinement, physical-system fidelity, and user acceptance remain
  outside the checked scope.
- Physical language on pp68-69 about forces that cannot resist motion is not
  promoted to a dynamics theorem by a zero-power or annihilator calculation.
  Constraints, contact model, admissible forces, and solution regularity must be
  added at their later source obligations.

## Appendix A Lie group and invariant-form obligations

Rows L05–L32 were inventoried by commit `c2bad4e` from MLS Appendix A (printed pp. 403–434) and
Exercise 17 of Chapter 2 (printed p. 78), read as text extracts of pp. 403–434 and 78 with pp. 428,
431 and 432 as rendered images. Carrier: forms on `se(3)` are `6 × 6` real matrices on twist
coordinates `(v, ω)`, `Ψ(ξ, η) = ξᵀ Ψ η` (p. 425), and invariance under change of frame is
`Ad_hᵀ Ψ Ad_h = Ψ` for every rigid transform `h` (A.11); a quadratic form on `SE(3)` is read as a
form on `se(3)` extended by left translation, tangent vectors at `g` being `4 × 4` matrices `g ξ̂`;
no manifold structure on `SO(n)`, `SE(3)` or `GL(n)` is built. Vector fields on matrix spaces use
Mathlib's bracket (the book's sign, p. 407) with the entrywise norm, and derivatives of the matrix
exponential the operator norm. Modules:
[InvariantMetrics](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/InvariantMetrics.lean),
[TwistForms](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/TwistForms.lean),
[LeftInvariantForms](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/LeftInvariantForms.lean),
[HyperbolicKilling](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/HyperbolicKilling.lean),
[KillingVolumeForm](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/KillingVolumeForm.lean),
[ReciprocalScrewSystems](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/ReciprocalScrewSystems.lean),
[JacobianFrames](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/JacobianFrames.lean),
[LeftInvariantFields](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/LeftInvariantFields.lean),
[MatrixExponential](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/MatrixExponential.lean),
[CanonicalCoordinates](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/CanonicalCoordinates.lean),
[GroupActions](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/GroupActions.lean) and
[ExponentialClosedForms](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/ExponentialClosedForms.lean).
Namespaces `InvariantMetric`, `Twist` and `LieGroup` below are under `RoboLean`. Rows L60–L72 were inventoried by commit `70996af` from printed pp. 408–416 and 427–433, read as text
with p. 409 as a rendered image. Carrier for them: the book's Lie groups are sets of real square
matrices, subgroups of `GL(n, ℝ)`, and the Lie algebra of such a set `G` is the set of matrices `A`
with `exp(tA) ∈ G` for every real `t` (`LieGroup.matrixLieAlgebra`); the dimension of a matrix Lie
group is the dimension of that Lie algebra; `GL(n, ℝ)` as a Lie group in Mathlib's sense is the unit
group of the endomorphisms of `ℝⁿ`, identified with the invertible matrices; one-forms live on real
normed spaces as the vector fields of Chapter 7 do. Modules:
[MatrixLieGroup](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/MatrixLieGroup.lean),
[LeftTranslation](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/LeftTranslation.lean),
[Dimension](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/Dimension.lean),
[LieExponential](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/LieExponential.lean),
[Manifold](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/Manifold.lean),
[ManifoldBracket](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/ManifoldBracket.lean),
[Haar](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/Haar.lean),
[LeftTranslationConstraints](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/LeftTranslationConstraints.lean) and
[OneForms](../../RoboLean/LieGroups/OneForms.lean).

Readings (derivations, not formalized): Proposition A.6 — the left invariant metrics of `SE(3)` correspond to all positive definite `6 × 6` matrices `Ψ_e`, a 21-parameter family, while an origin and a length scale are four parameters; the forms invariant under the rotations about a point `q` are, in a frame with origin `q`, `[[αI, βI], [βI, γI]]` with `α, γ > 0` and `αγ > β²` (by Lemma A.2, L06, applied to each block), and the printed parameterization is that of the subfamily `β = 0` up to an overall factor. ## First kinematic example and reusable obligations, Chapter 3

The future example is a planar two-revolute specialization of Example 3.1's SCARA
construction. Preserve zero-pose links along `+y`, set `l₀=θ₃=θ₄=0`, and write
lengths `a,b` and angles `q₁,q₂`. The target position is
`(-a sin q₁-b sin(q₁+q₂), a cos q₁+b cos(q₁+q₂), 0)` and orientation is
`Rz(q₁+q₂)`. This selected specialization is not a claim that MLS names that
exact two-link example. Real angles are a convenient coordinate lift; periodicity
must be established before identifying configurations with a torus.

The annulus theorem for positive lengths and unrestricted joints is a derived design
target, not a quoted theorem from the inspected pages; rows C01–C07 in
[Design certificates beyond MLS](#design-certificates-beyond-mls) now cover both
inclusions, zero radius, and equal lengths. Joint limits,
collision avoidance, continuous IK selection, and motion feasibility are separate. The complete workspace definitions (3.11)–(3.13) (p. 95) are rows K14–K16, and the planar
three-link annulus of Example 3.4 is K46. The joint-space structure `Q = Tᵖ × ℝʳ` and the sign
convention of p. 84 ("an angle about a directed axis is positive if it represents a clockwise
rotation as viewed along the direction of the axis") are K01 and K08 with the right-hand rule of
[the conventions](geometry-conventions.md): viewed along the axis direction, from behind, a
right-handed rotation is clockwise. The spherical-wrist workspace remark (p. 96) is K67, Exercise 13(b)–(c) is K69 and the count of
Subproblem 4's three spheres (Exercise 6) is K68. Parts (b)–(e) of Exercises 20–21 and 22(d) are K70–K77, and Exercise 3 for the four manipulators of
Figure 3.23 is K78–K81: (a) and (c) for all four (the body Jacobian of Figure 3.23(ii) open) and (b)
for (i) and, at the level of tool positions, (iii) and (iv). Exercise 2 ("the
forward kinematics map … is independent of the order in which rotations and translations are
performed") is read through p. 87, where `g_st(θ)` "gives the configuration of the tool frame
independently of the order in which the rotations and translations are actually performed": moving
the joints one at a time in any order reaches the product of exponentials, which is K05
(`SerialChain.toolPose_runMoves_perm`, for every chain). Exercise 3(b)–(c) for Figure 3.23(ii) is K90. Exercise 4 for the four manipulators of Figure 3.24 is
K82–K88 and K96: the inverse elbow (ii) and the Rhino (iv) read from the figure, and the elbow manipulator
(i) and the Stanford arm (iii) read as the arms of Examples 3.2 and 3.9 (with K28, K32, K49 and K67),
the figure drawing their wrists in the order `−x`, `+z`, `+y` where Figures 3.4 and 3.14 have `+z`,
`−x`, `+y`. Exercise 5 is K89, Exercise 7 is K91, and Exercises 9, 10, 11 and 12 are K94, K92, K95 and
K93. Not inventoried in Chapter 3: Exercise 1 (drawings of the twist axes of the manipulators of
Chapter 1, a request with no stated result). Chapter 3 has no Exercise 23.

### Design certificates beyond MLS

These rows are design statements from [the assessment](mls-lean-assessment.md)
("Robot design and workspace coverage"), not results printed in MLS. They use the
reachable workspace of p95 eq3.12 for the planar
two-link specialization `Examples.planarTwoLink a b` (K06–K07). MLS Example 3.4
(pp96-97) describes the analogous two-link annulus
only informally, as a step of a three-link construction in another frame, and
p98, eq3.16, prints the closed-form inverse kinematics
`θ₂ = π ± α` with the remark that no solution exists for `r > l₁ + l₂` (found in a
review of the formalization); the workspace equality and the certificates below are not printed. The C rows are
counted separately from the 196 MLS selected obligations. Rows C09 and C10 come from the Veil pilot (commit `9c8b539`): a supervisor model whose first-evaluation recipe is in [veil-robotics-verification.md](veil-robotics-verification.md), not from MLS or the assessment. Rows C11 and C12 come from the second Veil pilot (commit `7e752fe`), which extends the C09 supervisor with an integer command age to test Veil's proof reconstruction on arithmetic; not from MLS or the assessment. Rows C13 and C14 come from the third Veil pilot (commit `bd7b9e8`), which extends the C11 supervisor with a per-target admission count, two tick counters and a tick budget to test Veil's proof reconstruction on arithmetic under quantifiers, sums and truncated subtraction; not from MLS or the assessment.

Rows C15 and C16 come from
the fourth Veil pilot (commit `aa74623`), which extends the C13 supervisor with cost counters and a round-robin
scheduler to find where Veil's proof reconstruction stops (products of unknowns, `div` and `mod`,
model size); not from MLS or the assessment. Rows C17 and C18 come from the fifth Veil pilot
(commit `44a91b2`), which re-encodes the C15
scheduler without `div` and `mod` to test whether the fourth pilot's reconstruction failures go away; not from
MLS or the assessment.
Rows C19–C25 come from the planar arm demo (commit `b254787`, [planar-arm-demo.md](planar-arm-demo.md)): an executable mirror of the C11 timeout supervisor over rational targets and its refinement to the design relation; not from MLS or the assessment. Rows C26 and C27 come from the demo's Veil run and differential test (commit `7975d6c`): the C11 Veil model on the demo's instance and a test of the executable against Veil's executable semantics; not from MLS or the assessment. Row C28 comes from the demo's arrival-time statements (commit `5a650af`): the ideal continuous arm's convergence to each commanded set point joined to the executable's run invariants; not from MLS or the assessment.

Selected by commit `18f4de2` from Chapter 4,
printed pp. 155–178 (PDF 173–196): 24 obligations, 16 Verified in I11 and 8 open. This is a
selected inventory, not a measure of Chapter 4 or of the book. Lean link `k : Fin n` is the
book's link `k + 1` and Lean joint `j` the book's joint `j + 1`. Modules:

[MassMatrix](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/MassMatrix.lean),
[Christoffel](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/Christoffel.lean),
[PlanarTwoLinkDynamics](../../RoboLean/Examples/PlanarTwoLinkDynamics.lean).

## Chapter 5 grasp obligations

Selected by commit `cc0fd5f`
from Chapter 5 §§2–3, printed pp. 214–228 (PDF 232–246), with the force-closure claim of p. 242:
14 obligations, all Verified in I21. This is a selected inventory, not a measure of Chapter 5 or of
the book; §§4–6 are not inventoried. Lean coefficient `j` of contact `i` is the book's
`f^{j+1}_{c_{i+1}}`. Modules: [FrictionCone](../../RoboLean/Grasp/FrictionCone.lean),
[ForceClosure](../../RoboLean/Grasp/ForceClosure.lean), [Contact](../../RoboLean/Grasp/Contact.lean),
[GraspMap](../../RoboLean/Grasp/GraspMap.lean), [Frictionless](../../RoboLean/Grasp/Frictionless.lean),
[PlanarGrasp](../../RoboLean/Examples/PlanarGrasp.lean), [BoxGrasp](../../RoboLean/Examples/BoxGrasp.lean).
Every force-closure statement assumes unbounded contact forces at maintained rigid contacts
(MLS p. 214); none concerns actuator limits, contact persistence or a physical hand.

Rows G62–G72 were selected by commit `c28081b` from Chapter 5 §6.3, printed pp. 253–255, with Exercises
14, 15 and 17, pp. 262–263: 11 obligations, all Verified in I36. Modules:
[ContactBijection](../../RoboLean/Grasp/ContactBijection.lean),
[RollingHand](../../RoboLean/Grasp/RollingHand.lean),
[PlanarRegularContact](../../RoboLean/Grasp/PlanarRegularContact.lean),
[SurfaceOfRevolution](../../RoboLean/Examples/SurfaceOfRevolution.lean),
[PlanarEllipse](../../RoboLean/Examples/PlanarEllipse.lean), [RollingHand
(examples)](../../RoboLean/Examples/RollingHand.lean). The contact frame of a rolling hand is the contact
frame of §2 at the object's contact point (`z` along the inward normal), so the contact models of §2
apply unchanged. Nothing here concerns forces, friction, slip under dynamics or the persistence of
contact.

## Chapter 6 constrained dynamics obligations

Rows H01–H29 were inventoried by commit `d9b95e6`
from MLS Chapter 6 (printed pp. 265–316) following a digest of the chapter; §1
and §2 (pp. 265–285) were read as renders. The chapter contains one Lemma (6.1) and no Proposition; most rows
are numbered equations, prose definitions and examples. Carrier: configurations `Fin n → ℝ`
(`Q = ℝⁿ`) and a constraint field `A : (Fin n → ℝ) → Matrix (Fin k) (Fin n) ℝ`; the composite
hand–object configuration is `q ∈ Fin N → ℝ` relabeled by `e : Fin p ⊕ Fin n ≃ Fin N` into object
coordinates `x` and finger coordinates `θ`; `J_h` and `G` are abstract functions of `q`; for a `HandGrasp` with a chart of the object pose
they are derived from (5.15) (H30). d'Alembert's principle is a modeling assumption built into the definitions,
not derived. Existence and uniqueness of motions of a constrained system are not claimed anywhere.
Modules: [ConstrainedLagrangian](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/ConstrainedLagrangian.lean),
[CompositeDynamics](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/CompositeDynamics.lean),
[ConstrainedDynamics](../../RoboLean/Examples/ConstrainedDynamics.lean),
[HandDynamics](../../RoboLean/Examples/HandDynamics.lean); since commit `0361f5d` also
[PseudoInverse](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/PseudoInverse.lean), [RobotSystem](../../RoboLean/Control/RobotSystem.lean),
[HandControl](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/HandControl.lean), [RedundantDynamics](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/RedundantDynamics.lean),
[Tendons](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/Tendons.lean), [ObjectChart](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/ObjectChart.lean),
[GraspChart](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/GraspChart.lean), [StackedFingers](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/StackedFingers.lean),
[SubstitutedLagrangian](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/SubstitutedLagrangian.lean),
[RedundancyAndTendons](../../RoboLean/Examples/RedundancyAndTendons.lean) and [HandChart](../../RoboLean/Examples/HandChart.lean); since commit `1b9a28e` also [PoseChart](../../RoboLean/Dynamics/PoseChart.lean), [RobotControl](../../RoboLean/Control/RobotControl.lean), [RobotAttach](../../RoboLean/Control/RobotAttach.lean), [RobotAugmentedPD](../../RoboLean/Control/RobotAugmentedPD.lean) and the examples [PoseChart](../../RoboLean/Examples/PoseChart.lean), [RobotAttach](../../RoboLean/Examples/RobotAttach.lean), [RobotAugmentedPD](../../RoboLean/Examples/RobotAugmentedPD.lean).

## Chapter 7 nonholonomic obligations

Rows V01–V22 were inventoried by commit `6342e10` from MLS Chapter 7 (printed pp. 317–354), read as
text extracts of pp. 317–347 and 349–353 with pp. 325, 336, 340, 341 and 343 as rendered images.
Carrier: vector fields `f : E → E` on a real normed space `E` (MLS works in `ℝⁿ`, p. 321;
`Fin n → ℝ` is used in the examples); the bracket is Mathlib's `VectorField.lieBracket ℝ f g`,
`[f, g](q) = Dg(q) f(q) − Df(q) g(q)`, the book's sign (p. 324). Smoothness ("smooth" throughout
the chapter) is an explicit hypothesis per statement: `C²` at the point for the Jacobi identity and
the Lie-derivative identity, differentiability at the point for the product rule and the
integrability argument, `C^∞` generators for the filtration exercises and for the named statements
of Frobenius and Chow. Distributions are pointwise subspaces `Δ_q`; flows of fields with a bounded continuous derivative are constructed since commit `8b52cdc`, with
the group property, the inverse flow and commuting flows for a vanishing bracket (rows V24 and
V25); Theorem 7.2's sufficiency and Theorem 7.5 remain named propositions, not proved (the book
proves neither). Since commit `a574f74`, Theorem 7.2's sufficiency is proved with `C¹` defining maps (rows V26–V32, finite-dimensional `E`), the named proposition with `C^∞` defining maps was open at that commit. Since commit `70613b9`, Theorem 7.5 is proved on finite-dimensional spaces with unconstrained inputs (rows V14 and V50–V55), with Proposition 7.6's conclusion under the rank condition at the point and controllability from the rank condition at every point. Since commit `a2a55d2`, Theorem 7.2's sufficiency with smooth defining maps (`FrobeniusSufficiency E`) is proved on finite-dimensional spaces (rows V10 and V80–V83), from flows of class `C^k` in the initial state for every `k` and two-sided flows smooth in the time and the state. Controls are
piecewise constant. Modules: [VectorField](../../RoboLean/Nonholonomic/VectorField.lean),
[Distribution](../../RoboLean/Nonholonomic/Distribution.lean),
[Filtration](../../RoboLean/Nonholonomic/Filtration.lean),

## Chapter 8 nonholonomic steering obligations

Rows W01–W21 were inventoried by commit `66b2eb0` from MLS Chapter 8 (printed pp. 355–394), read as
text extracts of pp. 358–375, 382–387 and 391–394 with pp. 360, 371, 385 and 387 as rendered
images. The book calls most of the chapter approximate or informal (p. 371: "somewhat informal");
the rows select its exact statements: the model systems (Brockett's system (8.2), its `m`-input
form (8.4)–(8.5), the one-chain system (8.7) and Engel's system), Lemma 8.1, Propositions 8.2
and 8.3, the displacement formulas of Algorithm 3 and of p. 363, the stationary inputs of (8.3) with a
corrected printing, (8.11)–(8.16) and Proposition 8.4 under the necessary conditions, Exercise 6,
Example 8.3 (as printed, and corrected for (7.14)), (8.30)–(8.31), (8.34)–(8.36), Theorem 8.6 for
coordinate rectangles and the equation of Proposition 8.7. Carriers: `Fin n → ℝ` for the model
systems (the book's `qᵢ` is entry `i − 1`), a real normed space with multipliers in its dual for
§3.3. Trajectories are those of `IsTrajectory` (continuous on `[0, 1]`, the equation away from
finitely many times) with sinusoidal inputs, not piecewise constant ones; the steering statements
hold for every trajectory from every initial state, and trajectories exist for continuous inputs.

`K = diag(3/4, 3)`, `T = 0`), a concrete rolling motion of that ellipsoid on the plane,
`α_f(s) = (π, s/√(3/8))`, `α_o(s) = (0, −s)`, `ψ = 0`, which satisfies every hypothesis of Exercise
15(b) at `t = 0` and gives `ω_x = 3`, `ω_y = 0` by Exercise 15(c); a circular cylinder, whose
coordinate lines are lines of curvature with principal curvatures `1 ≠ 0`; the symmetric matrix
field `[[α₁, 1], [1, 0]]`; the plane chart of Example 5.7 as one- and two-patch atlases; and a
constant contact configuration of the ellipsoid on the plane described in one finger chart twice.
`OrthogonalChartStatement` is a statement only.

Decisions and readings. (1) The three-axis ellipsoid is charted by confocal coordinates `μ ∈ [b², a²]`,
`ν ∈ [c², b²]`, reparametrized by `μ = b² + (a² − b²) sin² s`, `ν = c² + (b² − c²) sin² t` so that the
chart is smooth and regular at the vertices `(±a, 0, 0)`, where the confocal coordinates themselves are
singular; it is an orthogonal chart wherever `sin s ≠ 0` or `cos t ≠ 0`, and the geometric parameters
are computed on the patch `{cos t > 0}`. That this patch covers, on `(−π, π] × (−π/2, π/2)`, the
ellipsoid without the two arcs of `x²/a² + z²/c² = 1` in the plane `y = 0` that join the umbilics
through `(0, 0, ±c)` is a derivation, not proved. (2) The curvature tensor is computed from the normal field `(x/a², y/b², z/c²)`, not by
differentiating the normalized cross product: this is the level-set reading of Exercise 19, whose test,
an ellipsoid rolling on a plane, is Exercise 15(b). (3) The semi-axes of Exercise 15 satisfy
`a > b > c` with the longest axis facing the object, as drawn. (4) The contact set of two bodies is
defined for atlases indexed by arbitrary types, with overlapping patches, as coinciding points with
opposite normals. (5) Theorem 5.11 transfers across a change of finger chart given the frame angle
along the motion as a function with a derivative; for the object chart the transfer is stated for
the relative pose. (6) Theorem 5.9 is a named statement with smooth charts and a smooth injective
reparametrization onto a neighbourhood; its proof needs first integrals of two transverse line fields,
which the library's composed-flow box (`C¹`, V28) does not provide. (7) An umbilic is defined (the book
does not use the word) and the principal frame is stated for symmetric matrix fields.

What is not claimed: a proof of Theorem 5.9; a chart-free form of (5.28) for level sets; smoothness of
`W`; the existence of a differentiable frame angle for smooth changes of chart; any statement about a
physical fingertip, friction or the persistence of contact.

point [Main](../../RoboLean/Cell/Main.lean) is not imported. Sources read as text extracts of
printed pp. 89–91, 161–162, 165, 168–175, 183–184, 190–195, 300–301 and 303, where the docstrings
cite MLS; the task's scene, cells, loop, supervisor, policy, configurations and bounds are design
statements. **Verified - library build and audit:** at commit `c5b7cc2`, on Lean 4.35.0 with
Mathlib v4.35.0 (moved by commits `aa06bca` and `88bb0d8`), `lake build` of the 481 modules
imported by `RoboLean.lean` exits 0 (4004 jobs), and the whole-library audit over those 481
modules reports 13017 constants, each depending on at most `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound` (10206 on all three, 854 on none), with 0 disallowed axioms, no `axiom` declaration
and no `opaque` stand-in; the declarations named in rows C30–C46 are among them. **Satisfying
instances:** the demonstration run (C36, C40), the disturbance step at which the acceleration
jumps (C37, C40), the idle program on encoder samples (C42), the held payload (C44), the arm at
rest with a mass error of `1` kg held by friction at both gains (C45, C46) and the demonstration
run with the model equal to the plant (C45) each meet every hypothesis of the theorem it
instantiates; C39 is a run that meets every hypothesis but the contract and violates the
conclusion. **Tested, not proved:** C47, the line protocol, by the replay of commit `2443d4f`.
**Veil-side, outside this library:** C48, checked in the Veil project at the re-pins of its
library requirement to the commits `88bb0d8`, `2443d4f`, `57aba61`, `da97b43` and `c5b7cc2`, and,
for the composite file as it stood at the move of both projects to one Lean release on
2026-11-06, by a fresh kernel replay of its environment. Design decisions adopted: the supervisor's fault permanent (a protective stop); the
contract stated with core imports only so that the same text elaborates in both projects; the
earlier hand-proved theorems kept beside the contract form; the position and the velocity of the
motion required to have right derivatives only; measured samples handled by widening the arrival
tolerances, every conclusion about the true motion; the plant assumption first as an acceleration
bound, then as a torque bound per joint, then derived from a payload and friction, and finally
from the controller's model with the rotor inertia and the nominal payload against the plant's
mass error, rotor-inertia error and friction, under one linear condition per gain; two design
points, the gains `80` and `50` rad/s with the tube radius `3/100` rad. Physical fidelity, the
existence of closed-loop solutions, the compiled program beyond its Lean definitions, numerics and
user acceptance remain Unverified; the MuJoCo evaluation under `demo/cell/` is a simulation, not
evidence for these rows.

## Source evidence and cautions

The inspected local PDF has SHA-256
`c85b9e1b9465789812edb750254fc88faff2b1557763e7cf1aa1e85307fc4a02`.
Chapter 2 pp23-38 were extracted/read. Selected Chapter 3 passages were read at
pp83-89,95,115-122. Rendered pages 26,30,35,37,87,89,115,118 were visually
inspected, including page labels and matrix/sign conventions. The source-inspection notes were prepared for
the first increment; they are distinct from Lean proof evidence.

Three source cautions remain explicit:

1. R17: the nonunit Rodrigues display divides by `‖ω‖`; I3 now proves the
   explicit nonzero formula and a separate zero case.
2. R19-R20: rendered p30 eq2.18 divides by `sin θ`, while prose excludes only
   `θ=0`. A half-turn also has zero sine. This is a missing case of that displayed
   construction, not evidence against exponential surjectivity.
3. R25-R28: p33's quaternion group prose needs nonzero input; p34 uses unit
   quaternions for rotations. Reverse axis extraction also needs endpoint cases;
   it cannot yield a global single-valued smooth inverse.

These source cautions are mathematical inferences from inspected formulas.
I3 checks R17's explicit nonzero and zero cases. I5 checks rotation existence
without a sine denominator and generic axis recovery only under its explicit
nonzero-sine premise; it does not validate the printed extraction at a half turn.
I6 restricts quaternion group claims to the norm-one carrier; quaternion
rotation and half-angle bridges R27-R28 remain Unverified. No correction
silently replaces a printed statement. Proof evidence must identify Lean/mathlib v4.34.1 and exact checks;
a build alone does not establish physical-model fidelity.

At I3, rendered printed pp27-31 and every page pp39-69 were
additionally opened. The preserved source review and P2 proposal record the
page ranges, commands, and normalization, zero-axis, signed-magnitude, and
reciprocity cautions. Appendix A brackets were not inspected in I3 and were outside I5. I6 now
records the separate bounded source inventory and four checked L rows.
